22.description: Saskatoon will provide a $2,000 sponsorship to the Japanese Association for their annual Japanese Children's Day event, which has been supported in previous years.

chips.text: Councillor questioned the $500 face painting cost, confirmed as typical.

21.description: Ali Abukar from Saskatoon Open Door Society shared details on upcoming events, including the National Day for the Child on February 28, 2026, and the Voice of Youth Leadership Summit on March 27, 2026.

chips.text: Saskatoon Open Door Society hosts events for youth and children.

16.description: Saskatoon paused the Living in Harmony Awards due to low engagement and reallocated $3,000 from its budget to member development and sponsorships.

chips.text: Teachers and schools faced capacity issues, leading to low awards engagement.
Staff questioned how the committee could support program growth and school involvement.

17.description: The Planning and Development Subcommittee is developing a new charter and planning its 2026 development day, seeking feedback on timing and topics.

chips.text: June is not a good month for non-profits due to AGMs.
The best time for the 2026 Planning Day remains undecided.

18.description: The Policy Advisory Subcommittee is tasked with drafting the 2026 Work Plan, which outlines the committee's goals and activities for the year. This plan must be submitted by March 31, 2026.

chips.text: Councillor Cheryl questioned the work plan's purpose and desired outcomes.
Subcommittee members Danielle, Brandon, Cheryl, and Alie are assigned the task.
It was unclear if the subcommittee chair must be decided at an official meeting.
The advisory manual, containing the mandate, will be sent to all committee members.
